## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
A clear parcel displaced along a θ_li surface has q_tot ≤ q_sat where it starts, so it can exceed saturation at the cell only by the amount q_sat falls along its path. On the surface θ_li is constant and q_sat changes with height alone, at the dry-adiabatic rate ∂_z q_sat|_ad (adiabatic_q_sat_gradient). The along-surface variance is therefore bounded by (∂_z q_sat|_ad)² ẑᵀD_cẑ, with ẑᵀD_cẑ = ℓ_v² ℓ_h² |∇_h θ|² / (nᵀDn) the vertical variance of the along-surface displacement.

The bound is zero on a flat surface, so stirring along the flat isentropes of the tropics adds no saturation excess, which is the advection–condensation result that condensation requires motion to lower q_sat. On sloped isentropes the bound is of order 0.1 q_sat in standard deviation and is rarely active. Unbounded, the Gaussian moist tail of the along-surface term condensed in humid tropical cells at every step, and the 1M scheme removed the water, drying the tropical troposphere.
